correctness.rationale: Exact Fourier Parseval identity yields a rational derivative. Its normalized positive-source terms have strictly negative log derivative with numerator at most -(1-t)^3. This yields precisely one global minimum. Strictly convex g_t(x)=x/(1-tx)^2 gives Jensen bias and convex-order monotonicity; the implicit-function derivative is positive and gives the claimed small-variance coefficient. The near-boundary equation converges uniformly to a strictly monotone scalar equation; a nonzero derivative yields O(epsilon^2) radius accuracy. Substituting into exact error gives the positive Laplace-transform integral and sharp inverse-epsilon minimized loss. Standalone packaged checker passed 91 finite diagnostics; not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The best single wrapped-Cauchy approximation to a mixed directional sample is an explicit mathematical problem in the 2019 thesis. Here the best-fit concentration is proved uniquely determined for arbitrary compact mixing probabilities, strictly biased upward with respect to the first Fourier coefficient, and strictly monotone under all mean-preserving spreads. A new sharp boundary-depth law shows that genuine mixture heterogeneity forces optimized squared error to diverge at an exact order with a positive computable coefficient. This supplies broadly useful structural and asymptotic information not provided by the prior stationary equation or gridded family preference maps.
